messages.text:
Greetings, I have a NexusQX1 (BM1370) would the nexus qx1 firmware upgrade work on this?  I apologize if this is a dumb question.

Thank you for your time

Nick
Searched the web · Nexus QX1 miner BM1370 firmware
Searched the web · Harlo OS firmware supported miners Nexus QX1 download harlol

Hello Nick,

Not a dumb question at all, and it is the right one to ask before you flash anything.

Short answer: yes. The N. QX1 is on the supported model list for Harlo OS, so the QX1 firmware image is the correct one for your unit. Your QX1 is the four chip BM1370 board, about 8.1 TH/s at roughly 170W, and the QX1 profile is built for exactly that board.

The one thing to be careful about is picking the profile by model name, not by chip family. Several other Nexus units (the S1 and S1-1, for example) run BM1373 chips, so a Nexus S1 image is not interchangeable with a QX1 image even though both say Nexus on the box. Pick "Nexus QX1" in the flasher and nothing else.

How to do it: open harlolabs.com in Chrome or Edge, select Nexus QX1, connect the miner with a USB data cable (a charge only cable will not be seen), then install. If your unit is already running Harlo OS, take the OTA image and it keeps your wifi, your pools and your display settings. If it is on the firmware it shipped with, or you want a clean start, use the factory image, which erases saved settings so you will re-enter your pool and worker afterwards. It takes about two minutes, then power it up and the self test runs on its own.

Before you start, it is worth opening the miner's web interface and noting your stratum URL, port and worker name so you can put them straight back in if you go the factory route. After the flash, give it a few minutes at its ramp up frequency before judging the hashrate, since the first averaging window always reads low and error rate reads high while the chips come up to speed.

If anything looks off during the flash, or you want to compare notes with other QX1 owners, the Harlo Labs Discord is the fastest place: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , and JD, who builds Harlo OS, is @nullhashrate there. Happy to keep helping here too if you tell me what version the unit reports once it boots.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
